The AI Revolution: Who Wins, Who Loses & the SaaSpocalypse | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 70

Dan Ives and Gil Luria argue for an extended AI buildout while differentiating infrastructure, model and application economics. Eisman challenges capital intensity, weak model moats and Chinese price competition. The episode contains genuine Ives/Luria Oracle revisions, conditional Apple and cybersecurity theses, and overbroad guest claims about software debt and productivity necessarily creating jobs. Eisman retains model-moat doubts in his closing recap.

Conditional reasoning

Removing a model-license charge does not remove the arithmetic, storage or electricity needed to run inference. This supports distinct value-chain exposure, not identical spending per task or assured provider profit.

Wrong
Source · 48:24-49:00 ↗
SpeakerGil Luria
Stanceasserted
Horizonnot stated
Materialitymajor

The claimed necessity does not follow from microeconomics; demand response and prices matter.

Conditional reasoning

Required employment falls from Q/a to Q/(2a) while revenue remains price times Q. This counterexample disproves the claimed necessary doubling of revenue and hiring. Expanded demand can instead increase employment, but requires additional assumptions.

  • Consider a firm facing fixed demand Q and fixed price.
  • Output per worker rises from a to 2a.
